name: 22q11.2 Deletion Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical diagnosis confirmed by genetic testing

criteria.description: Hemizygous deletion of chromosome 22q11.2 detected by FISH, MLPA, chromosomal microarray, or other molecular method
Conotruncal cardiac defect (tetralogy of Fallot, interrupted aortic arch, truncus arteriosus, VSD)
Palatal abnormalities (velopharyngeal insufficiency, cleft palate, submucous cleft)
Characteristic facial features (long face, hooded eyelids, bulbous nasal tip, small ears)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Detection of 22q11.2 deletion by molecular genetics. Clinical suspicion based on typical features triggers testing.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Most common microdeletion syndrome in humans. ~90% have a ~3 Mb deletion; ~8% have a ~1.5 Mb deletion. TBX1 is the critical gene. ~90-95% are de novo; ~5-10% inherited from an affected parent.

common.notes: Tetralogy of Fallot (20%), VSD, interrupted aortic arch type B, truncus arteriosus
Long face, hooded eyelids, broad nasal bridge, bulbous nasal tip, small low-set ears

occasional.notes: From hypoparathyroidism; may present as neonatal seizures
Ranges from mild T-cell lymphopenia to severe combined immunodeficiency (complete DiGeorge, rare)

rare.notes: ~25-fold increased risk compared to general population; onset typically late adolescence/young adulthood

rare.symptomName: Autoimmune disorders (JIA, ITP, autoimmune thyroid disease)

laboratory: Low serum calcium and elevated phosphorus (hypoparathyroidism)
Low T-cell counts (especially CD4+ naive T cells)
Absent or reduced T-cell receptor excision circles (TRECs) on newborn screening
Low absolute lymphocyte count in neonates
imaging: Renal ultrasound may show structural anomalies
Chest X-ray may show absent thymic shadow in neonates
Brain MRI may show polymicrogyria or white matter abnormalities
genetic: 22q11.2 deletion detected by chromosomal microarray (preferred first-line test)
TBX1 is the critical haploinsufficient gene
other: Immune function panel (lymphocyte subsets, mitogen stimulation)

distinguishingFeatures: CHARGE has coloboma and choanal atresia
Peripheral pulmonary stenosis rather than conotruncal defects

redFlags: Severe T-cell immunodeficiency (complete DiGeorge - medical emergency)
Complex congenital heart disease requiring surgical repair
Development of psychotic symptoms in adolescence/young adulthood
references: McDonald-McGinn DM, et al. 22q11.2 deletion syndrome. Nat Rev Dis Primers. 2015;1:15071.
Bassett AS, et al. Practical guidelines for managing patients with 22q11.2 deletion syndrome. J Pediatr. 2011;159(2):332-339.e1.
Sullivan KE. Chromosome 22q11.2 deletion syndrome and DiGeorge syndrome. Immunol Rev. 2019;287(1):186-201.
Schneider M, et al. Psychiatric disorders from childhood to adulthood in 22q11.2 deletion syndrome. Am J Psychiatry. 2014;171(6):627-639.
